applicability: Historical: the response bytes of GET /api/notes/list (removed). Current: the per-folder properties above for GET /api/notes/folder.
conditions: The notes tree is not mutated between the two listings being compared.
Depth is counted on the lexical path, so an in-root directory symlink is listed and pruned at its own position.
exclusions: A directory that is readable but not searchable, reached directly or through an in-root symlink: its children are skipped and the listing answers 200 where the path-based walk answered 500 (Architect rulings 2026-09-28T16:30:31 and 16:55:00).
A directory renamed out of the notes root while it is being listed: its own entries are still listed through the open descriptor, where the path-based walk lost it.
Error answers other than the ELOOP/ENOTDIR swap signature and the is_dir errno set, which propagate exactly as before (for example a mode-000 directory still answers 500).
statement: Dated L55 bound for the superseded endpoint: GET /api/notes/list returned the same bytes as before the bounding change (files before folders by case-folded name with readdir-order ties; in-root symlinks under their own lexical path; escaping/broken symlinks and non-regular files skipped; depth-4 pruning with truncated true; missing folder as empty list). The endpoint is removed by the accepted packet; current per-folder properties (in-root aliases under their own path, escaping/broken skips, missing-folder emptiness) hold in list_folder and are governed by the rule 2 entry — except ordering (directories-first, exact-name ties) and the envelope, which differ.
